question.text: A highly rigid cubical block <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> of small mass <math><mi>M</mi></math> and side <math><mi>L</mi></math> is fixed rigidly on to another cubical block <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> of the same dimensions and of low modulus of rigidity <math><mi>η</mi></math> such that the lower face of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> completely covers the upper face of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>. The lower face of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is rigidly held on a horizontal surface. A small force <math><mi>F</mi></math> is applied perpendicular to one of the side faces of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>. After the force is withdrawn, block <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> executes small oscillations, the time period of which is given by
